## Shell Configuration Structure Report

### How Files Are Loaded

Both `~/.zshrc.tmpl` and `~/.bashrc.tmpl` use the same `load_modular_dir()` function (lines 109-118 in zshrc; lines 78-89 in bashrc):
- **Glob pattern**: `$dir/*.$ext` (sorted alphabetically)
- **Naming convention**: Numeric prefix (00, 01, 02…) ensures deterministic load order
- **Shared POSIX layer**: Both shells call `load_modular_dir "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell" sh` to load all `.sh` files
- **Shell-specific layer**: zsh loads `$ZSH_CONFIG_DIR/*.zsh` and `$ZSH_CONFIG_DIR/tools/*.zsh`; bash loads `$BASH_CONFIG_DIR/*.bash`

### Shell Modules in dot_config/shell/

All 21 `.sh` / `.sh.tmpl` files are POSIX-portable, sourced by **both** shells. No naming prefix is enforced; they're just sorted:

**Shell dispatch pattern** (10 files use it): Check `[ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]` or `[ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]` at source time, then call the appropriate tool init (starship, fzf, atuin, zoxide, etc.). Example from 01_starship.sh (lines 8-12):
```bash
if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
    eval "$(starship init zsh)"
elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
    eval "$(starship init bash)"
fi
```

98	        print -r -- "${agent:-claude}"
99	        return
100	    fi
101	    case "$agent" in
102	        ""|"specstory")
103	            # No agent specified → bare `specstory run` (default = claude).
104	            print -r -- "specstory run"
105	            ;;
106	        claude|codex|cursor|droid|gemini)
107	            print -r -- "specstory run $agent"
108	            ;;
109	        *)
110	            # Pass-through for non-specstory providers (opencode today, more
111	            # later as specstory adds support).
112	            print -r -- "$agent"
113	            ;;
114	    esac
115	}
116	
117	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
118	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
119	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
120	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
121	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
122	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
123	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
124	#             land in shell.
125	#
126	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
127	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
128	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
129	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
130	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
131	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
132	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
133	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
134	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
135	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
136	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
137	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
138	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
139	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
140	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
141	    case "$mode" in
142	        kill)
143	            print -r -- "$inner"
144	            ;;
145	        restart)
146	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
147	            print -r -- "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
148	            ;;
149	        shell|*)
150	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
151	            # terminals tmux supports.
152	            print -r -- "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
153	            ;;
154	    esac
155	}
156	
157	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
158	# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
159	# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
160	# launch nvim manually inside the new session.
161	#
162	# Smart argument handling:
163	#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
164	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
165	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
166	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
167	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
168	function sesh-here() {
169	    local cmd="" target=""
170	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
171	        case "$1" in
172	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
173	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
174	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
175	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
176	        esac
177	    done
178	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
179	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
180	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
181	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
182	    else
183	        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
184	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
185	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
186	        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
187	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
188	        local session
189	        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
190	        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
191	        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
192	    fi
193	}
194	
195	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
196	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
197	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
198	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
199	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
200	function sesh-root() {
201	    local cmd="" root
202	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
203	        case "$1" in
204	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
205	            -*)           shift ;;
206	            *)            break ;;
207	        esac
208	    done
209	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
210	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
211	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
212	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
213	    else
214	        sesh connect "$root"
215	    fi
216	}
217	
218	alias shere='sesh-here'
219	alias sroot='sesh-root'
220	alias scode='sesh-code'
221	alias svibe='sesh-vibe'
222	
223	# ── scode: repo-aware coding-agent layout ───────────────────────────────────
224	#
225	# Open the coding-agent layout (nvim 75% | specstory-wrapped agent 25%, btop
226	# window) in a session NAMED FOR THE CURRENT REPO, so different repos don't
227	# collide on the single `coding-agent` session name.
228	#
229	# Session naming:
230	#   In repo /Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/foo  → session `coding-agent/foo`
231	#   Same repo re-invocation                     → attach (no duplicate)
232	#   Different repo                              → new session `coding-agent/<other>`
233	#
234	# Outside a git repo the function refuses with a hint to use `shere` or `svibe`
235	# (the heavy layout doesn't make sense for ad-hoc directories).
236	#
237	# Agent wrapping: known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini)
238	# are auto-wrapped in `specstory run X` for markdown auto-save. Others
239	# (opencode today) pass through raw — see _sesh_wrap_agent + backlog entry
240	# `specstory-opencode-support` for the upstream tracking.
241	#
242	# Exit behavior: `--on-exit shell` (default) drops to a shell with a hint when
243	# the agent exits, so Ctrl+C doesn't kill the pane. Use `--on-exit kill` for
244	# the old behavior, or `--on-exit restart` for an auto-respawn loop.
245	#
246	# Usage:
247	#   scode                              # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
248	#   scode codex                        # specstory run codex
249	#   scode opencode                     # opencode raw (not yet a specstory provider)
250	#   scode --on-exit kill claude        # Ctrl+C kills the right pane
251	#   scode --on-exit restart codex      # codex auto-respawns on crash
252	#   scode -p ~/some/other/repo         # explicit repo path
253	#   scode --no-attach                  # create session in background, don't switch
254	function sesh-code() {
255	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
256	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
257	        case "$1" in
258	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
259	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
260	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
261	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
262	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
263	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
264	            --agents)
265	                echo "scode: --agents is svibe-only (scode is single-agent)." >&2
266	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: svibe --agents '$2'" >&2
267	                return 1 ;;
268	            -h|--help)
269	                cat <<'EOF'
270	scode — open repo-scoped coding-agent layout
271	
272	Usage: scode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
273	             [--no-attach] [AGENT]
274	
275	Layout: window `editor` (nvim 75% | agent 25%) + window `monitor` (btop).
276	Session name: `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (one session per repo).
277	Requires:     git repo (errors otherwise — use `shere` or `svibe`).
278	
279	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
280	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
281	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
282	
283	--on-exit MODE controls what happens when ANY pane command exits/Ctrl+C
284	(applies to the agent pane, the nvim pane, and the btop monitor window):
285	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
286	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
287	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
288	
289	Examples:
290	  scode                            # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
291	  scode codex                      # right pane: specstory run codex
292	  scode opencode                   # right pane: opencode (raw)
293	  scode --no-specstory claude      # right pane: claude (raw, no markdown auto-save)
294	  scode --on-exit kill claude      # right pane closes when claude exits
295	  scode -p ~/work/foo              # explicit repo path
296	EOF
297	                return 0 ;;
298	            -*)             echo "scode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
299	            *)              [[ -z "$agent" ]] && agent="$1" || true; shift ;;
300	        esac
301	    done
302	
303	    case "$on_exit" in
304	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
305	        *) echo "scode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
306	    esac
307	
308	    # Resolve repo root
309	    local repo_root
310	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
311	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
312	    else
313	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
314	    fi
315	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
316	        echo "scode: not inside a git repo." >&2
317	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell, or \`svibe\` for a vibe layout in any dir." >&2
318	        return 1
319	    fi
320	
321	    # Validate agent CLI exists in PATH (fail-fast). Specstory itself isn't
322	    # checked here — if the user passed a known provider but specstory is
323	    # missing, the pane will exit with specstory's error message and
324	    # --on-exit=shell will leave a shell to read it.
325	    if [[ -n "$agent" ]] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
326	        echo "scode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
327	        return 1
328	    fi
329	
330	    local repo_name session
331	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
332	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")
333	
334	    # If session already exists, just attach (idempotent — solves the
335	    # cross-repo collision problem the old single `coding-agent` session had).
336	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
337	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
338	        return 0
339	    fi
340	
341	    # Create session + build layout directly with tmux commands (see svibe
342	    # comment block for why not tmuxp).
343	    #
344	    # Window 1 "editor": nvim (left, will be 75%) | wrapped agent (right, 25%)
345	    # Window 2 "monitor": btop (or htop / top fallback)
346	    local agent_inner agent_cmd
347	    agent_inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$agent" "$specstory_mode")
348	    agent_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$agent_inner" "$on_exit" "${agent:-agent}")
349	
350	    # nvim and monitor get the same on-exit treatment as the agent so that
351	    # quitting them drops to a shell with a re-launch hint instead of the
352	    # pane/window vanishing.
353	    local nvim_cmd monitor_inner monitor_cmd
354	    nvim_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
355	
356	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
357	    tmux split-window -h -t "${session}:editor" -c "$repo_root" "$agent_cmd"
358	    # main-vertical layout, then size the LEFT pane to 75% of window width
359	    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:editor" main-vertical >/dev/null
360	    tmux resize-pane -t "${session}:editor.1" -x 75% 2>/dev/null
361	
362	    # Monitor window
363	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=btop
364	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=htop
365	    else                                       monitor_inner=top
366	    fi
367	    monitor_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$monitor_inner" "$on_exit" "$monitor_inner")
368	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n monitor -c "$repo_root" "$monitor_cmd"
369	
370	    # Focus editor window, left (nvim) pane
371	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:editor"
372	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:editor.1"
373	
374	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
375	}
376	
377	# ── svibe: parametric multi-agent vibe layout ───────────────────────────────
378	#
379	# A "vibe coding" session: window 1 has N agent panes (default 4), window 2
380	# is lazygit, window 3 is nvim. Built directly with tmux split/new-window
381	# commands so it stays parametric (tmuxp YAML can't express dynamic pane counts).
382	#
383	# Session naming: `vibe/<dir-basename>` — collision-safe across directories.
384	# Refuses outside a git repo (use `shere` for plain shells in arbitrary dirs).
385	#
386	# Each agent pane is wrapped in `specstory run X` (for known providers, opt
387	# out with --no-specstory) and additionally wrapped in an exit handler
388	# controlled by `--on-exit MODE` — same semantics as `scode`. Default `shell`
389	# keeps the pane open with a hint after the agent exits, so Ctrl+C is
390	# recoverable.
391	#
392	# Two modes for choosing which agents run:
393	#   1. Homogeneous (positional): `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all running codex
394	#   2. Heterogeneous (--agents):  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
395	#                                 → 4 panes running those specific agents
396	#                                 (list LENGTH determines pane count;
397	#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
398	#                                 ambiguity)
399	#
400	# Usage:
401	#   svibe                                          # 4× claude (specstory)
402	#   svibe 2                                        # 2× claude
403	#   svibe 4 codex                                  # 4× specstory run codex
404	#   svibe 3 opencode                               # 3× opencode (raw)
405	#   svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode     # 4 panes, mixed
406	#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
407	#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
408	#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
409	#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
410	#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background
411	function sesh-vibe() {
412	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
413	    local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
414	    local agent_cli="claude"
415	    local agents_csv=""
416	    local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
417	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
418	        case "$1" in
419	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
420	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
421	            --agents)       agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
422	            --min-width)    min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
423	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
424	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
425	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
426	            -h|--help)
427	                cat <<'EOF'
428	svibe — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
429	
430	Usage:
431	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
432	        [--min-width COLS] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
433	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
434	        [--min-width COLS] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
435	
436	Default: svibe           (N auto-picked from term_width ÷ min-width, clamp [1,12])
437	  window 1 "agents" — N agent panes (columns if all fit at ≥min-width, else tiled)
438	  window 2 "git"    — lazygit
439	  window 3 "edit"   — nvim
440	
441	Two modes for choosing agents:
442	  Homogeneous:    `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all codex
443	  Heterogeneous:  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
444	                  → 4 panes (one each, in order); list length = pane count
445	
446	Session name: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (collision-safe per directory).
447	Requires:     git repo (use `shere` for plain shells elsewhere).
448	
449	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
450	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
451	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
452	
453	--on-exit MODE controls per-pane behavior on Ctrl+C / clean exit
454	(applies to all agent panes, the lazygit window, and the nvim window):
455	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
456	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
457	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
458	
459	--min-width COLS sets the minimum readable per-pane width (default: value of
460	$SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80). It drives two decisions:
461	  • auto-pick N when you don't pass a count (N = term_width / min-width)
462	  • columns vs tiled in the agents window: columns when all N panes fit at
463	    ≥COLS wide side-by-side, otherwise tiled grid
464	Example on a 240-col terminal:
465	  min-width 80   → auto N=3, three even-horizontal columns
466	  min-width 120  → auto N=2, two even-horizontal columns
467	
468	Examples:
469	  svibe                                            # auto N × claude, width-aware layout
470	  svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
471	  svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
472	  svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy)
473	  svibe --min-width 120                            # wider panes → fewer auto columns
474	  svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
475	  svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill    # 2 panes, mixed
476	  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
477	EOF
478	                return 0 ;;
479	            -*)             echo "svibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
480	            *)              break ;;
481	        esac
482	    done
483	
484	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
485	        echo "svibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
486	        return 1
487	    fi
488	
489	    # Current terminal width, used for auto-picking N (when the user didn't
490	    # pass a count) and for the columns-vs-tiled cutover. $COLUMNS is
491	    # auto-maintained by zsh on SIGWINCH; tput is a fallback for corner cases
492	    # (e.g. non-interactive invocation); 200 is a generous last resort.
493	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
494	
495	    # Build the agents array. Two paths:
496	    #   --agents claude,codex,…  → split csv, list length = pane count
497	    #   positional [N] [CLI]     → repeat CLI N times (N auto-picked if omitted)
498	    # Mixing both is rejected to keep semantics unambiguous.
499	    local -a agents
500	    if [[ -n "$agents_csv" ]]; then
501	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
502	            echo "svibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
503	            echo "       Pick one. (e.g. drop the trailing args)" >&2
504	            return 1
505	        fi
506	        # Split CSV. Trim whitespace per element so 'claude, codex' works.
507	        local IFS=','
508	        agents=( ${=agents_csv} )
509	        # Trim leading/trailing whitespace on each element
510	        local j
511	        for (( j = 1; j <= ${#agents}; j++ )); do
512	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]## }"
513	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]%% }"
514	        done
515	        if (( ${#agents} == 0 )); then
516	            echo "svibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
517	            return 1
518	        fi
519	    else
520	        # Positional: [n_agents] [agent_cli]
521	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
522	            if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
523	                n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
524	            fi
525	        fi
526	        [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && agent_cli="$1"
527	
528	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width when the user didn't pass one.
529	        # N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12). On a 240-col terminal
530	        # with min-width 80 that's N=3; at min-width 120, N=2.
531	        if (( ! n_agents_set )); then
532	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
533	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
534	            (( n_agents > 12 )) && n_agents=12
535	        fi
536	
537	        # Build a homogeneous array of length n_agents
538	        local k
539	        for (( k = 1; k <= n_agents; k++ )); do
540	            agents+=( "$agent_cli" )
541	        done
542	    fi
543	
544	    case "$on_exit" in
545	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
546	        *) echo "svibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
547	    esac
548	
549	    if (( ${#agents} < 1 || ${#agents} > 12 )); then
550	        echo "svibe: agent count = ${#agents} out of range [1, 12]" >&2
551	        return 1
552	    fi
553	
554	    # Resolve repo root
555	    local repo_root
556	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
557	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
558	    else
559	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
560	    fi
561	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
562	        echo "svibe: not inside a git repo." >&2
563	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell in arbitrary directories." >&2
564	        return 1
565	    fi
566	
567	    # Validate ALL agent CLIs exist in PATH (fail-fast — we don't want to
568	    # build a 4-pane layout where one pane is dead). De-dup the list to keep
569	    # the error message readable.
570	    local -a missing
571	    local -A seen
572	    local a
573	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
574	        [[ -n "${seen[$a]:-}" ]] && continue
575	        seen[$a]=1
576	        if ! command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
577	            missing+=( "$a" )
578	        fi
579	    done
580	    if (( ${#missing} > 0 )); then
581	        echo "svibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH: ${missing[*]}" >&2
582	        echo "       Available: $(for c in claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini; do command -v $c >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo -n "$c "; done)" >&2
583	        return 1
584	    fi
585	
586	    local repo_name session
587	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
588	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
589	
590	    # Idempotent: existing session = just attach
591	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
592	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
593	        return 0
594	    fi
595	
596	    # Build wrapped command for each agent (the wrapping is pane-specific so
597	    # we can mix providers in one window).
598	    #
599	    # Helper: turn agent name → fully-wrapped tmux command string.
600	    _vibe_agent_cmd() {
601	        local inner
602	        inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
603	        _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
604	    }
605	
606	    # ── Build the session ───────────────────────────────────────────────
607	    # Window 1: agents (start with first pane running agents[1])
608	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
609	        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"
610	
611	    # Pick window layout based on agent count vs what fits as readable
612	    # side-by-side columns at --min-width:
613	    #   N ≤ term_width / min_width → even-horizontal (columns)
614	    #   otherwise                  → tiled (grid — columns would be too narrow)
615	    local max_columns=$(( term_width / min_width ))
616	    (( max_columns < 1 )) && max_columns=1
617	    local svibe_layout
618	    if (( ${#agents} <= max_columns )); then
619	        svibe_layout="even-horizontal"
620	    else
621	        svibe_layout="tiled"
622	    fi
623	
624	    # Add remaining panes
625	    local i
626	    for (( i = 2; i <= ${#agents}; i++ )); do
627	        tmux split-window -t "${session}:agents" -c "$repo_root" \
628	            "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[$i]}")"
629	        # Re-balance after each split so layout stays uniform
630	        tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" "$svibe_layout" >/dev/null
631	    done
632	
633	    unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd
634	
635	    # Window 2: git (lazygit if present)
636	    # lazygit and nvim get the same on-exit handling as agents — quitting
637	    # them drops to shell with a re-launch hint rather than killing the window.
638	    local git_cmd edit_cmd
639	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
640	        git_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "lazygit" "$on_exit" "lazygit")
641	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "$git_cmd"
642	    else
643	        # `git status; exec $SHELL` already lands in shell — no wrap needed.
644	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "git status; exec \$SHELL"
645	    fi
646	
647	    # Window 3: edit (nvim)
648	    edit_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
649	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n edit -c "$repo_root" "$edit_cmd"
650	
651	    # Focus agents window, first pane
652	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:agents"
653	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:agents.1"
654	
655	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
656	}
657	
658	# Register as zsh widget
659	zle -N sesh-sessions
660	
661	# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
662	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
663	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
664	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions
665

```text
# 22_sesh.zsh - sesh tmux session manager
# https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh

# Check if sesh is installed
command -v sesh &>/dev/null || return 0

# Auto-generate shell completion into ~/.zfunc/ (regenerates on version change)
if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
    local _sesh_ver="$(sesh --version 2>/dev/null)"
    if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_sesh ]] || ! grep -q "${_sesh_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null; then
        sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null
    fi
fi

# Sesh session switcher with fzf (full-featured picker)
# Supports icons, preview, filtering by source, and session killing
function sesh-sessions() {
    {
        exec </dev/tty
        exec <&1
        local session
        session=$(sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
            --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
            --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
            --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
            --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
            --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
            --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
            --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
            --preview-window 'right:55%' \
            --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
        )
        zle reset-prompt > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
        [[ -z "$session" ]] && return
        sesh connect "$session"
    }
}

# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# All helpers below take care to avoid the lowercase `path` / `cdpath` /
# `manpath` / `fpath` zsh-tied-array trap (see
# pitfalls/zsh-tied-array-path-shadowing.md).

# Resolve the git repo root, or return non-zero if not in a repo.
function _sesh_git_root() {
    git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null
}

# Sanitize a string for use as a tmux session name.
# tmux forbids `.` and `:` in session names; we also strip whitespace.
function _sesh_sanitize() {
    print -r -- "${1//[.:[:space:]]/-}"
}

# Switch to or attach to a tmux session named $1 (creating it at $2 if needed).
# Inside tmux: `switch-client`. Outside tmux: `attach-session`.
function _sesh_attach_or_switch() {
    local session="$1"
    if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
        tmux switch-client -t "$session"
    else
        tmux attach-session -t "$session"
    fi
}

# Create (or no-op if exists) a detached tmux session at the given path.
# Returns 0 if the session already existed, 1 if newly created. (Caller uses
# this to decide whether to apply layout setup or just attach.)
function _sesh_ensure_session() {
    local session="$1" target="$2"
    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0   # already exists
    fi
    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$target"
    return 1       # newly created
}

# Wrap a known specstory provider in `specstory run X` so the agent picks up
# auto-save markdown logging. Bare CLI names that aren't specstory providers
# (currently: opencode — see backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md) pass
# through unchanged.
#
# Update the case list when specstory adds providers (track upstream:
# specstoryai/getspecstory#146 for opencode, similar issues for others).
#
# Args: $1=agent, $2=specstory_mode (auto|never; default auto)
#   auto  — wrap if known provider, raw otherwise (the historical default)
#   never — pass through raw regardless (CLI flag --no-specstory sets this)
function _sesh_wrap_agent() {
    local agent="$1" specstory_mode="${2:-auto}"
    if [[ "$specstory_mode" == "never" ]]; then
        # Even an empty agent goes raw → caller's responsibility to pick a
        # sensible default (we choose `claude` upstream when --no-specstory
        # is set, since `specstory run` with no arg defaults to claude too).
        print -r -- "${agent:-claude}"
        return
    fi
    case "$agent" in
        ""|"specstory")
            # No agent specified → bare `specstory run` (default = claude).
            print -r -- "specstory run"
            ;;
        claude|codex|cursor|droid|gemini)
            print -r -- "specstory run $agent"
            ;;
        *)
            # Pass-through for non-specstory providers (opencode today, more
            # later as specstory adds support).
            print -r -- "$agent"
            ;;
    esac
}

# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
#             land in shell.
#
# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
    local guard="trap '' INT;"
    case "$mode" in
        kill)
            print -r -- "$inner"
            ;;
        restart)
            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
            print -r -- "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
            ;;
        shell|*)
            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
            # terminals tmux supports.
            print -r -- "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
            ;;
    esac
}

# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
# launch nvim manually inside the new session.
#
# Smart argument handling:
#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
function sesh-here() {
    local cmd="" target=""
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
        esac
    done
    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
    target="${target:-$PWD}"
    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
    else
        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
        local session
        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
    fi
}

# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
#   sroot                              # default startup_command
#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
function sesh-root() {
    local cmd="" root
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -*)           shift ;;
            *)            break ;;
        esac
    done
    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
    else
        sesh connect "$root"
    fi
}

alias shere='sesh-here'
alias sroot='sesh-root'
alias scode='sesh-code'
alias svibe='sesh-vibe'

# ── scode: repo-aware coding-agent layout ───────────────────────────────────
#
# Open the coding-agent layout (nvim 75% | specstory-wrapped agent 25%, btop
# window) in a session NAMED FOR THE CURRENT REPO, so different repos don't
# collide on the single `coding-agent` session name.
#
# Session naming:
#   In repo /Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/foo  → session `coding-agent/foo`
#   Same repo re-invocation                     → attach (no duplicate)
#   Different repo                              → new session `coding-agent/<other>`
#
# Outside a git repo the function refuses with a hint to use `shere` or `svibe`
# (the heavy layout doesn't make sense for ad-hoc directories).
#
# Agent wrapping: known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini)
# are auto-wrapped in `specstory run X` for markdown auto-save. Others
# (opencode today) pass through raw — see _sesh_wrap_agent + backlog entry
# `specstory-opencode-support` for the upstream tracking.
#
# Exit behavior: `--on-exit shell` (default) drops to a shell with a hint when
# the agent exits, so Ctrl+C doesn't kill the pane. Use `--on-exit kill` for
# the old behavior, or `--on-exit restart` for an auto-respawn loop.
#
# Usage:
#   scode                              # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
#   scode codex                        # specstory run codex
#   scode opencode                     # opencode raw (not yet a specstory provider)
#   scode --on-exit kill claude        # Ctrl+C kills the right pane
#   scode --on-exit restart codex      # codex auto-respawns on crash
#   scode -p ~/some/other/repo         # explicit repo path
#   scode --no-attach                  # create session in background, don't switch
function sesh-code() {
    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
            --agents)
                echo "scode: --agents is svibe-only (scode is single-agent)." >&2
                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: svibe --agents '$2'" >&2
                return 1 ;;
            -h|--help)
                cat <<'EOF'
scode — open repo-scoped coding-agent layout

Usage: scode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
             [--no-attach] [AGENT]

Layout: window `editor` (nvim 75% | agent 25%) + window `monitor` (btop).
Session name: `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (one session per repo).
Requires:     git repo (errors otherwise — use `shere` or `svibe`).

Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough

--on-exit MODE controls what happens when ANY pane command exits/Ctrl+C
(applies to the agent pane, the nvim pane, and the btop monitor window):
  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop

Examples:
  scode                            # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
  scode codex                      # right pane: specstory run codex
  scode opencode                   # right pane: opencode (raw)
  scode --no-specstory claude      # right pane: claude (raw, no markdown auto-save)
  scode --on-exit kill claude      # right pane closes when claude exits
  scode -p ~/work/foo              # explicit repo path
EOF
                return 0 ;;
            -*)             echo "scode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
            *)              [[ -z "$agent" ]] && agent="$1" || true; shift ;;
        esac
    done

    case "$on_exit" in
        shell|kill|restart) ;;
        *) echo "scode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac

    # Resolve repo root
    local repo_root
    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
    else
        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
    fi
    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
        echo "scode: not inside a git repo." >&2
        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell, or \`svibe\` for a vibe layout in any dir." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Validate agent CLI exists in PATH (fail-fast). Specstory itself isn't
    # checked here — if the user passed a known provider but specstory is
    # missing, the pane will exit with specstory's error message and
    # --on-exit=shell will leave a shell to read it.
    if [[ -n "$agent" ]] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "scode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local repo_name session
    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")

    # If session already exists, just attach (idempotent — solves the
    # cross-repo collision problem the old single `coding-agent` session had).
    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
        return 0
    fi

    # Create session + build layout directly with tmux commands (see svibe
    # comment block for why not tmuxp).
    #
    # Window 1 "editor": nvim (left, will be 75%) | wrapped agent (right, 25%)
    # Window 2 "monitor": btop (or htop / top fallback)
    local agent_inner agent_cmd
    agent_inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$agent" "$specstory_mode")
    agent_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$agent_inner" "$on_exit" "${agent:-agent}")

    # nvim and monitor get the same on-exit treatment as the agent so that
    # quitting them drops to a shell with a re-launch hint instead of the
    # pane/window vanishing.
    local nvim_cmd monitor_inner monitor_cmd
    nvim_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")

    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
    tmux split-window -h -t "${session}:editor" -c "$repo_root" "$agent_cmd"
    # main-vertical layout, then size the LEFT pane to 75% of window width
    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:editor" main-vertical >/dev/null
    tmux resize-pane -t "${session}:editor.1" -x 75% 2>/dev/null

    # Monitor window
    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=btop
    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=htop
    else                                       monitor_inner=top
    fi
    monitor_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$monitor_inner" "$on_exit" "$monitor_inner")
    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n monitor -c "$repo_root" "$monitor_cmd"

    # Focus editor window, left (nvim) pane
    tmux select-window -t "${session}:editor"
    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:editor.1"

    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
}

# ── svibe: parametric multi-agent vibe layout ───────────────────────────────
#
# A "vibe coding" session: window 1 has N agent panes (default 4), window 2
# is lazygit, window 3 is nvim. Built directly with tmux split/new-window
# commands so it stays parametric (tmuxp YAML can't express dynamic pane counts).
#
# Session naming: `vibe/<dir-basename>` — collision-safe across directories.
# Refuses outside a git repo (use `shere` for plain shells in arbitrary dirs).
#
# Each agent pane is wrapped in `specstory run X` (for known providers, opt
# out with --no-specstory) and additionally wrapped in an exit handler
# controlled by `--on-exit MODE` — same semantics as `scode`. Default `shell`
# keeps the pane open with a hint after the agent exits, so Ctrl+C is
# recoverable.
#
# Two modes for choosing which agents run:
#   1. Homogeneous (positional): `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all running codex
#   2. Heterogeneous (--agents):  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
#                                 → 4 panes running those specific agents
#                                 (list LENGTH determines pane count;
#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
#                                 ambiguity)
#
# Usage:
#   svibe                                          # 4× claude (specstory)
#   svibe 2                                        # 2× claude
#   svibe 4 codex                                  # 4× specstory run codex
#   svibe 3 opencode                               # 3× opencode (raw)
#   svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode     # 4 panes, mixed
#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background
function sesh-vibe() {
    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
    local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
    local agent_cli="claude"
    local agents_csv=""
    local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --agents)       agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --min-width)    min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
            -h|--help)
                cat <<'EOF'
svibe — parametric multi-agent vibe layout

Usage:
  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
        [--min-width COLS] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
        [--min-width COLS] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]

Default: svibe           (N auto-picked from term_width ÷ min-width, clamp [1,12])
  window 1 "agents" — N agent panes (columns if all fit at ≥min-width, else tiled)
  window 2 "git"    — lazygit
  window 3 "edit"   — nvim

Two modes for choosing agents:
  Homogeneous:    `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all codex
  Heterogeneous:  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
                  → 4 panes (one each, in order); list length = pane count

Session name: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (collision-safe per directory).
Requires:     git repo (use `shere` for plain shells elsewhere).

Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough

--on-exit MODE controls per-pane behavior on Ctrl+C / clean exit
(applies to all agent panes, the lazygit window, and the nvim window):
  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop

--min-width COLS sets the minimum readable per-pane width (default: value of
$SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80). It drives two decisions:
  • auto-pick N when you don't pass a count (N = term_width / min-width)
  • columns vs tiled in the agents window: columns when all N panes fit at
    ≥COLS wide side-by-side, otherwise tiled grid
Example on a 240-col terminal:
  min-width 80   → auto N=3, three even-horizontal columns
  min-width 120  → auto N=2, two even-horizontal columns

Examples:
  svibe                                            # auto N × claude, width-aware layout
  svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
  svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
  svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy)
  svibe --min-width 120                            # wider panes → fewer auto columns
  svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
  svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill    # 2 panes, mixed
  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
EOF
                return 0 ;;
            -*)             echo "svibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
            *)              break ;;
        esac
    done

    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
        echo "svibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Current terminal width, used for auto-picking N (when the user didn't
    # pass a count) and for the columns-vs-tiled cutover. $COLUMNS is
    # auto-maintained by zsh on SIGWINCH; tput is a fallback for corner cases
    # (e.g. non-interactive invocation); 200 is a generous last resort.
    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"

    # Build the agents array. Two paths:
    #   --agents claude,codex,…  → split csv, list length = pane count
    #   positional [N] [CLI]     → repeat CLI N times (N auto-picked if omitted)
    # Mixing both is rejected to keep semantics unambiguous.
    local -a agents
    if [[ -n "$agents_csv" ]]; then
        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
            echo "svibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
            echo "       Pick one. (e.g. drop the trailing args)" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        # Split CSV. Trim whitespace per element so 'claude, codex' works.
        local IFS=','
        agents=( ${=agents_csv} )
        # Trim leading/trailing whitespace on each element
        local j
        for (( j = 1; j <= ${#agents}; j++ )); do
            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]## }"
            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]%% }"
        done
        if (( ${#agents} == 0 )); then
            echo "svibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # Positional: [n_agents] [agent_cli]
        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
            if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
            fi
        fi
        [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && agent_cli="$1"

        # Auto-pick N from terminal width when the user didn't pass one.
        # N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12). On a 240-col terminal
        # with min-width 80 that's N=3; at min-width 120, N=2.
        if (( ! n_agents_set )); then
            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
            (( n_agents > 12 )) && n_agents=12
        fi

        # Build a homogeneous array of length n_agents
        local k
        for (( k = 1; k <= n_agents; k++ )); do
            agents+=( "$agent_cli" )
        done
    fi

    case "$on_exit" in
        shell|kill|restart) ;;
        *) echo "svibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac

    if (( ${#agents} < 1 || ${#agents} > 12 )); then
        echo "svibe: agent count = ${#agents} out of range [1, 12]" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Resolve repo root
    local repo_root
    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
    else
        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
    fi
    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
        echo "svibe: not inside a git repo." >&2
        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell in arbitrary directories." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Validate ALL agent CLIs exist in PATH (fail-fast — we don't want to
    # build a 4-pane layout where one pane is dead). De-dup the list to keep
    # the error message readable.
    local -a missing
    local -A seen
    local a
    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
        [[ -n "${seen[$a]:-}" ]] && continue
        seen[$a]=1
        if ! command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            missing+=( "$a" )
        fi
    done
    if (( ${#missing} > 0 )); then
        echo "svibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH: ${missing[*]}" >&2
        echo "       Available: $(for c in claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini; do command -v $c >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo -n "$c "; done)" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local repo_name session
    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")

    # Idempotent: existing session = just attach
    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
        return 0
    fi

    # Build wrapped command for each agent (the wrapping is pane-specific so
    # we can mix providers in one window).
    #
    # Helper: turn agent name → fully-wrapped tmux command string.
    _vibe_agent_cmd() {
        local inner
        inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
        _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
    }

    # ── Build the session ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Window 1: agents (start with first pane running agents[1])
    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"

    # Pick window layout based on agent count vs what fits as readable
    # side-by-side columns at --min-width:
    #   N ≤ term_width / min_width → even-horizontal (columns)
    #   otherwise                  → tiled (grid — columns would be too narrow)
    local max_columns=$(( term_width / min_width ))
    (( max_columns < 1 )) && max_columns=1
    local svibe_layout
    if (( ${#agents} <= max_columns )); then
        svibe_layout="even-horizontal"
    else
        svibe_layout="tiled"
    fi

    # Add remaining panes
    local i
    for (( i = 2; i <= ${#agents}; i++ )); do
        tmux split-window -t "${session}:agents" -c "$repo_root" \
            "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[$i]}")"
        # Re-balance after each split so layout stays uniform
        tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" "$svibe_layout" >/dev/null
    done

    unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd

    # Window 2: git (lazygit if present)
    # lazygit and nvim get the same on-exit handling as agents — quitting
    # them drops to shell with a re-launch hint rather than killing the window.
    local git_cmd edit_cmd
    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        git_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "lazygit" "$on_exit" "lazygit")
        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "$git_cmd"
    else
        # `git status; exec $SHELL` already lands in shell — no wrap needed.
        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "git status; exec \$SHELL"
    fi

    # Window 3: edit (nvim)
    edit_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n edit -c "$repo_root" "$edit_cmd"

    # Focus agents window, first pane
    tmux select-window -t "${session}:agents"
    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:agents.1"

    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
}

# Register as zsh widget
zle -N sesh-sessions

# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions
```

190	# --- claude-plans-here -----------------------------------------------------
191	# Scaffold or update project-local .claude/settings.json so Claude Code's
192	# /plan files land in ./.claude/plans/ (kept inside the repo) instead of the
193	# user-global plansDirectory. Pairs well with the agent-history-hygiene skill,
194	# which can then redact + commit the plan files alongside the diff.
195	#
196	# Also offers to import "orphan" plans — plans previously written under the
197	# global ~/.claude/plans/ that belong to this project. Detection: scan
198	# ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl (where Claude Code logs sessions
199	# per cwd; encoding maps '/' and '.' to '-') for Write/Edit tool_use entries
200	# whose file_path points into ~/.claude/plans/. This avoids false positives
201	# from sessions that merely *mentioned* a plan path in conversation.
202	#
203	# Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]
204	#   -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt
205	#   -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt
206	claude-plans-here() {
207		force_settings=0
208		force_orphans=0
209		while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
210			case "$1" in
211			-f) force_settings=1 ;;
212			-y) force_orphans=1 ;;
213			-h | --help)
214				echo "Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]"
215				echo "  -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt"
216				echo "  -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt"
217				return 0
218				;;
219			*)
220				echo "claude-plans-here: unknown flag '$1'" >&2
221				return 1
222				;;
223			esac
224			shift
225		done
226	
227		target=".claude/settings.json"
228		mkdir -p .claude/plans
229	
230		if [ ! -e "$target" ]; then
231			cat >"$target" <<'EOF'
232	{
233	  "plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"
234	}
235	EOF
236			echo "Wrote $PWD/$target"
237		else
238			if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
239				echo "claude-plans-here: jq required to merge into existing $target" >&2
240				return 1
241			fi
242	
243			ans=y
244			if [ "$force_settings" = "0" ]; then
245				printf '%s exists. Merge plansDirectory into it? [y/N] ' "$target"
246				read -r ans
247			fi
248	
249			case "$ans" in
250			y | Y | yes | YES | Yes)
251				tmp="$(mktemp)" || return 1
252				if jq --arg p "./.claude/plans" '. + {plansDirectory: $p}' "$target" >"$tmp"; then
253					mv "$tmp" "$target"
254					echo "Merged plansDirectory into $PWD/$target"
255				else
256					rm -f "$tmp"
257					echo "claude-plans-here: jq failed; $target unchanged" >&2
258					return 1
259				fi
260				;;
261			esac
262		fi
263	
264		_claude_plans_here_import_orphans "$force_orphans"
265		unset force_settings force_orphans target ans tmp
266	}
267	
268	# Internal: scan ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd|encoded-git-root>/*.jsonl
269	# for Write/Edit tool_use entries that wrote into ~/.claude/plans/, list the
270	# ones still living in the global dir and not yet copied locally, prompt y/N.
271	_claude_plans_here_import_orphans() {
272		force="$1"
273		global_plans="$HOME/.claude/plans"
274		[ -d "$global_plans" ] || return 0
275	
276		# Claude Code projects/ encoding: replace each '/' and '.' with '-'.
277		enc_cwd="$(printf '%s' "$PWD" | tr '/.' '--')"
278		enc_root=""
279		if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
280			groot="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
281			if [ -n "$groot" ] && [ "$groot" != "$PWD" ]; then
282				enc_root="$(printf '%s' "$groot" | tr '/.' '--')"
283			fi
284		fi
285	
286		proj_dirs=""
287		[ -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_cwd" ] && proj_dirs="$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_cwd"
288		[ -n "$enc_root" ] && [ -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root" ] &&
289			proj_dirs="$proj_dirs $HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root"
290		[ -z "$proj_dirs" ] && return 0
291	
292		jsonl_files=""
293		for d in $proj_dirs; do
294			for f in "$d"/*.jsonl; do
295				[ -r "$f" ] || continue
296				jsonl_files="$jsonl_files $f"
297			done
298		done
299		[ -z "$jsonl_files" ] && return 0
300	
301		# Two-stage filter: only lines containing a Write/Edit tool_use, then
302		# extract any plan-path within them. Authoritative — avoids matching plan
303		# paths that merely appeared in user/assistant text.
304		re_prefix="$(printf '%s' "$global_plans" | sed 's/[.[\*^$()+?{|]/\\&/g')"
305		matches="$(
306			# shellcheck disable=SC2086
307			grep -hE '"name":"(Write|Edit)"' $jsonl_files 2>/dev/null |
308				grep -oE "${re_prefix}/[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+\.md" |
309				sort -u
310		)"
311		[ -z "$matches" ] && return 0
312	
313		candidates=""
314		count=0
315		while IFS= read -r m; do
316			[ -f "$m" ] || continue
317			base="${m##*/}"
318			[ -e ".claude/plans/$base" ] && continue
319			candidates="$candidates
320	$m"
321			count=$((count + 1))
322		done <<EOF
323	$matches
324	EOF
325		[ "$count" = 0 ] && return 0
326	
327		echo
328		echo "Found $count orphan plan(s) in ~/.claude/plans/ linked to this project:"
329		printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | while IFS= read -r m; do
330			[ -z "$m" ] && continue
331			printf '  - %s\n' "${m#$HOME/}"
332		done
333	
334		ans=y
335		if [ "$force" = "0" ]; then
336			printf 'Copy them into ./.claude/plans/ (originals kept)? [y/N] '
337			read -r ans
338		fi
339		case "$ans" in
340		y | Y | yes | YES | Yes) ;;
341		*) return 0 ;;
342		esac
343	
344		copied=0
345		printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | while IFS= read -r m; do
346			[ -z "$m" ] && continue
347			cp -n "$m" .claude/plans/ 2>/dev/null && copied=$((copied + 1))
348		done
349		echo "Copied plan(s) into $PWD/.claude/plans/"
350		unset force global_plans enc_cwd enc_root proj_dirs jsonl_files re_prefix matches candidates count m base ans copied
351	}

1	# 15_atuin.sh — atuin (https://atuin.sh) shared init for zsh + bash.
2	# Loaded by both shells via load_modular_dir; shell-specific bits dispatch
3	# on $ZSH_VERSION / $BASH_VERSION at source time.
4	#
5	# Decisions (see TODO.md "atuin zsh asymmetry" + docs/tools/atuin.md):
6	#   - macOS: brew installs to /opt/homebrew/bin (already on PATH).
7	#   - Linux: official installer (https://setup.atuin.sh) writes to
8	#     ~/.atuin/bin/atuin. Ansible role atuin runs the installer with
9	#     ATUIN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 so we own the PATH wiring here.
10	#   - zsh: Ctrl+R stays on fzf-history-widget (muscle memory). Atuin
11	#     binds to Alt+R via _atuin_search_widget. Up-arrow stays on OMZ
12	#     history-substring-search (no atuin rebind).
13	#   - bash: Ctrl+R = atuin (long-standing in dot_bashrc.tmpl); Alt+R
14	#     also = atuin for cross-shell consistency. Up-arrow disabled
15	#     because ble.sh owns it.
16	#   - Local-only by default. Sync requires manual `atuin login -u …`
17	#     (see docs/tools/atuin.md → Opt-in sync).
18	
19	# --- PATH wiring (Linux installer location) ----------------------------------
20	[ -d "$HOME/.atuin/bin" ] && export PATH="$HOME/.atuin/bin:$PATH"
21	
22	# --- Presence gate -----------------------------------------------------------
23	command -v atuin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
24	
25	# --- zsh init ----------------------------------------------------------------
26	# We do NOT bind Ctrl+R or Up-arrow on zsh (preserve fzf + OMZ widgets).
27	# zsh-vi-mode wipes bindkeys on init, so dot_zshrc.tmpl's zvm_after_init
28	# re-sources THIS file to re-apply the Alt+R bind.
29	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
30	    if eval "$(atuin init zsh --disable-up-arrow --disable-ctrl-r)" 2>/dev/null; then
31	        # _atuin_search_widget is registered by `atuin init zsh`.
32	        # Bind Alt+R (\er) to it across all keymaps that zsh-vi-mode uses.
33	        if (( ${+widgets[_atuin_search_widget]} )); then
34	            bindkey -M emacs '\er' _atuin_search_widget
35	            bindkey -M viins '\er' _atuin_search_widget
36	            bindkey -M vicmd '\er' _atuin_search_widget
37	        fi
38	    fi
39	    return 0
40	fi

3	# Load if any media tool is on PATH (installMediaTools=true, or hand-installed).

10	# === ffmpeg helpers (video / audio) =========================================
11	
12	# Compress an MP4 with x264 CRF 28 (smaller; tweak CRF inline for quality).
13	# Output: <name>_compressed.mp4 next to the input.
14	compress-video() {
15	    emulate -L zsh
16	    [[ -f "$1" ]] || { echo "usage: compress-video <input>" >&2; return 2 }
17	    ffmpeg -i "$1" -c:v libx264 -crf 28 -preset slow -c:a aac -b:a 128k "${1:r}_compressed.mp4"
18	}
19	
20	# Extract audio without re-encoding. Output is .m4a (AAC sources keep AAC).
21	extract-audio() {
22	    emulate -L zsh
23	    [[ -f "$1" ]] || { echo "usage: extract-audio <input>" >&2; return 2 }
24	    ffmpeg -i "$1" -vn -c:a copy "${1:r}.m4a"
25	}
26	
27	# Re-encode to 16 kHz mono WAV — Whisper / faster-whisper / wav2vec input format.
28	to-wav16k() {
29	    emulate -L zsh
30	    [[ -f "$1" ]] || { echo "usage: to-wav16k <input>" >&2; return 2 }
31	    ffmpeg -i "$1" -ar 16000 -ac 1 "${1:r}_16k.wav"
32	}
33	
34	# === ImageMagick helpers (image) ============================================
35	
36	# Resolve `magick` (v7) or `convert` (v6) into $REPLY. Returns 1 if neither.
37	_29_media_im() {
38	    REPLY=$(command -v magick) && return 0
39	    REPLY=$(command -v convert) && return 0
40	    echo "ImageMagick not found (install via installMediaTools=true)" >&2
41	    return 1
42	}
43	
44	# compress-image <input> [<target_mb=1>]
45	# Re-encode to JPEG under <target_mb> MB. Uses ImageMagick's
46	# `-define jpeg:extent=NMB`, which iterates quality internally — single shot,
47	# no manual binary search. Alpha is flattened to white (PNG/WebP screenshots).
48	# Output: <name>_<mb>mb.jpg
49	compress-image() {
50	    emulate -L zsh
51	    [[ -f "$1" ]] || { echo "usage: compress-image <input> [<target_mb=1>]" >&2; return 2 }
52	    local IM; _29_media_im || return 1; IM=$REPLY
53	    local mb="${2:-1}"
54	    local out="${1:r}_${mb}mb.jpg"
55	    "$IM" "$1" -auto-orient -strip -background white -alpha remove -alpha off \
56	        -define "jpeg:extent=${mb}MB" "$out"
57	    [[ -f "$out" ]] && echo "→ $out ($(du -h "$out" | cut -f1))"
58	}
59	
60	# resize-image <input> <width_px>
61	# Resize so width = <width_px> (preserves aspect). Output keeps source format.
62	# Output: <name>_<width>w.<ext>
63	resize-image() {
64	    emulate -L zsh
65	    [[ -f "$1" && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "usage: resize-image <input> <width_px>" >&2; return 2 }
66	    local IM; _29_media_im || return 1; IM=$REPLY
67	    local out="${1:r}_${2}w.${1:e}"
68	    "$IM" "$1" -auto-orient -resize "${2}x" "$out"
69	    [[ -f "$out" ]] && echo "→ $out ($(du -h "$out" | cut -f1))"
70	}

76	    # No-args entrypoint that wires every helper above for non-CLI users.
77	    media-pick() {

79	        local file action
80	        file=$(gum file --no-permissions) || return 0
81	        [[ -f "$file" ]] || { echo "not a file: $file" >&2; return 2 }
82	        action=$(gum choose \
83	            "compress-video" \
84	            "compress-image (1 MB)" \
85	            "compress-image (custom MB)" \
86	            "resize-image (custom width)" \
87	            "extract-audio" \

92	            "compress-image (custom MB)")

100	                resize-image "$file" "$w"

102	            "extract-audio")             extract-audio "$file" ;;
103	            "to-wav16k")                 to-wav16k "$file" ;;

==> /Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh <==
# OSC 133 shell integration — emits prompt/command markers so tmux can
# navigate command boundaries (next-prompt / previous-prompt in copy-mode)
# and the prefix + M-y binding in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf can
# copy the last command's output (Warp-style).
#
# Protocol: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md
#
#   OSC 133 ; A ST             before prompt (start of prompt)
#   OSC 133 ; B ST             between prompt and command input (end of prompt)
#   OSC 133 ; C ST             after Enter, before command output (start of output)
#   OSC 133 ; D ; exit_code ST after command finishes (end of output)
#
# Uses add-zsh-hook so it chains cleanly after starship / zsh-vi-mode / oh-my-zsh
# (they all also use add-zsh-hook — no clobbering).
#
# Opt-out: export DISABLE_OSC133=1 before starting zsh.

[[ -n "$DISABLE_OSC133" ]] && return
[[ "$TERM" == "dumb" ]] && return

autoload -Uz add-zsh-hook

_osc133_precmd() {
  local ec=$?
  # Wrap the (already-rendered-by-starship) PROMPT with D + A markers using
  # %{...%} so zsh treats them as zero-width. This runs AFTER starship's
  # own precmd (add-zsh-hook chains in registration order; 01_starship.zsh
  # loads before 02_shell_integration.zsh).
  #
  # Why in PROMPT, not printf? An earlier version printf'd A from precmd
  # directly. tmux's OSC 133 line-attr tracking was unreliable — ZLE's
  # cursor management between precmd and prompt-paint caused the A flag
  # to land on the wrong grid line (next-prompt navigation found zero A
  # markers even though the bytes were sent). Embedding via PROMPT
  # guarantees the markers render at the exact spatial location tmux
  # expects (start of the prompt line).
  #
  # D marker carries the previous command's exit code; A marks start of
  # new prompt. Neither is strictly required for next-prompt/previous-prompt
  # navigation (A is, D isn't), but both are cheap.
  PROMPT=$'%{\e]133;D;'"${ec}"$';\a\e]133;A\a%}'"${PROMPT}"
}

_osc133_preexec() {
  # Skip C for our own tmux capture helpers — otherwise their copy-mode
  # `previous-prompt -o` chain lands on their own (empty) output start
  # instead of the previous command's real output. Coupling is documented
  # in 03_tmux_capture.zsh.
  case "${1%% *}" in
    cpout|cpcmd|cpblock) return ;;

# 96_ssh_setup.zsh - Interactive SSH key setup for remote machines
#
# Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host
#
# Walks through: create key → ssh-copy-id → copy key to remote → add SSH config entries.
# See docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md for the full tutorial.

ssh-setup-remote() {
  emulate -L zsh
  setopt localoptions pipefail

  local usage="Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host"
  if (( $# != 1 )); then
    print -u2 -- "$usage"
    return 1
  fi

  local target="$1"
  local remote_user remote_host
  if [[ "$target" == *@* ]]; then
    remote_user="${target%%@*}"
    remote_host="${target#*@}"
  else
    remote_host="$target"
    remote_user=""
  fi

  # ── Step 0: Key selection ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  print "\n=== SSH Key Setup for $target ==="

  local key_path=""
  local create_new=""

  print "\nExisting keys in ~/.ssh/:"
  local -a existing_keys=()
  for f in ~/.ssh/*.pub(N); do
    existing_keys+=("${f%.pub}")
    print "  ${f%.pub}"
  done

  if (( ${#existing_keys} > 0 )); then
    print -n "\nUse an existing key? [Y/n] "
    read -r create_new
    if [[ "$create_new" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then
      create_new="yes"
    else
      print -n "Enter key path (without .pub): "
      read -r key_path
      # Expand ~ manually
      key_path="${key_path/#\~/$HOME}"

3	# Priority order:

7	#

9	# one agent instead of spawning a new one each time.

11	# Probe timeout (seconds) — keeps shell startup fast even when an agent
12	# socket exists but the daemon behind it is hung or locked.

15	# Wrapper: ssh-add -l with a timeout to avoid hanging on unresponsive sockets.
16	# Returns the same exit codes as ssh-add -l (0, 1, 2) plus 124 for timeout.
17	_ssh_add_probe() {
18	    if command -v timeout &>/dev/null; then
19	        timeout "$_SSH_AGENT_PROBE_TIMEOUT" ssh-add -l "$@" 2>&1
20	    else
21	        # No timeout command (rare) — run directly and hope for the best
22	        ssh-add -l "$@" 2>&1
23	    fi
24	}

31

40	            "$HOME/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
41	            "$HOME/snap/bitwarden/current/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
42	            "$HOME/.var/app/com.bitwarden.desktop/data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
43	        )
44	    fi
45	
46	    for _sock in "${_bw_candidates[@]}"; do
47	        if [[ -S "$_sock" ]]; then
48	            # Socket file exists — verify the agent actually responds
49	            local _out
50	            _out="$(SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$_sock" _ssh_add_probe)"
51	            local rc=$?
52	            # rc=0: keys listed  → usable
53	            # rc=1 + "no identities": agent ok, no keys loaded → usable
54	            # rc=1 + "refused": Bitwarden locked/agent disabled → skip
55	            # rc=2: agent unreachable → skip
56	            # rc=124: timed out → skip
57	            if (( rc == 0 )); then
58	                export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$_sock"
59	                return 0
60	            elif (( rc == 1 )) && [[ "$_out" != *"refused"* ]]; then
61	                export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$_sock"
62	                return 0

66	    return 1

81	        return 0
82	    fi

91	    local agent_sock="$agent_dir/agent.sock"

106	        fi

108	        rm -f "$agent_sock" "$agent_pid_file"
109	    fi
110	
111	    # Spawn a new agent with a fixed socket path
112	    mkdir -p "$agent_dir"
113	    chmod 700 "$agent_dir"
114	    eval "$(ssh-agent -a "$agent_sock" 2>/dev/null)" &>/dev/null
115	    if [[ -n "$SSH_AGENT_PID" ]]; then

117	        export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$agent_sock"

# Port `22_sesh.zsh` to shared shell layer + audit `dot_config/zsh/tools/`

## Context

`dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` (664 lines) defines five user-facing commands:

| Cmd | Alias | What |
|---|---|---|
| `sesh-sessions` | Alt+S | ZLE picker (fzf-tmux) over `sesh list` |
| `sesh-here` | `shere` | plain shell session at `$PWD` |
| `sesh-root` | `sroot` | shell session at git root |
| `sesh-code` | `scode` | repo-scoped `coding-agent/<repo>` layout (nvim + agent + btop) |
| `sesh-vibe` | `svibe` | parametric multi-agent vibe layout (N panes + lazygit + nvim) |

The Explore audit showed that ~95% of this file is plain shell logic. Only the **picker widget** (`sesh-sessions`, `zle -N`, `bindkey`) and the zsh-completion regeneration block are genuinely zsh-only. All other functions trip a small, mechanical list of zsh-isms: `print -r --`, `${=var}` word-splitting flag, 1-indexed array access (`${arr[1]}`), `${#arr}` array-length syntax, and one `local -A`.

Per CLAUDE.md's three-tier file placement rule and the documented pattern ("extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir"), the right shape is:

- shared backend in `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh`
- zsh ZLE wrapper in `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` (slim)
- bash ble.sh wrapper in `dot_config/bash/06_sesh.bash`

User decisions:
- **Bash 4+ baseline** for shared layer (keep `local -A`; bash 3.2 mac users running `svibe` ad-hoc will see runtime errors but no source-time breakage — acceptable).
- **Stage 1 = sesh** (this PR). **Full audit** with subsequent stages identified.
- **Alt+S ble.sh binding** included in Stage 1.

---

## Stage 1 (this PR): `22_sesh.zsh` split

### Files

**NEW** `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` — backend (~600 lines, sourced by both shells):

- Guard: `command -v sesh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0` at top
- All `_sesh_*` helpers: `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_attach_or_switch`, `_sesh_ensure_session`, `_sesh_wrap_agent`, `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`
- User-facing functions: `sesh-here`, `sesh-root`, `sesh-code`, `sesh-vibe`
- The 4 aliases: `shere`, `sroot`, `scode`, `svibe`
- `sesh-sessions` (the picker function body) — **moved here** so bash can call it too; the `zle reset-prompt` line is removed (it's a no-op-ish in ZLE-widget context anyway; both shells redraw on widget exit)

**MODIFIED** `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` — slim ZLE wrapper (~25 lines):

- Keep the `~/.zfunc/_sesh` completion-regeneration block (zsh-specific path)
- `zle -N sesh-sessions`
- 3× `bindkey -M {emacs,viins,vicmd} '\es' sesh-sessions`

**NEW** `dot_config/bash/06_sesh.bash` — ble.sh wrapper (~10 lines):

\```bash
# Bash Alt+S → sesh picker via ble.sh
# Backend (sesh-sessions function) lives in dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh
command -v sesh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
type ble-bind &>/dev/null || return 0   # only if ble.sh attached
ble-bind -m emacs   -x 'M-s' 'sesh-sessions'
ble-bind -m vi_imap -x 'M-s' 'sesh-sessions'
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -x 'M-s' 'sesh-sessions'
\```
(Exact `ble-bind` syntax: cross-reference existing patterns in `dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash.tmpl` and `dot_config/bash/05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl` during implementation.)

### Mechanical portability fixes (applied as we copy into `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh`)

1. **`print -r --` → `printf '%s\n'`** — 7 occurrences (lines 55, 98, 104, 107, 112, 143, 147, 152 of current file).
2. **`${=agents_csv}` (current line 508)** → `IFS=',' read -ra agents <<< "$agents_csv"` (works in zsh and bash 4+).
3. **`${#agents}` → `${#agents[@]}`** — zsh accepts both; bash needs `[@]`.
4. **1-indexed array access** — current code uses `${agents[1]}`, `agents[$j]`, etc. Rewrite to iterate without index access where possible:
   \```sh
   first_agent="${agents[0]}"   # bash-style; zsh with KSH_ARRAYS — see below
   for a in "${agents[@]}"; do … done
   \```
   For zsh+bash dual compatibility, gate the indexing with `setopt KSH_ARRAYS` locally in zsh:
   \```sh
   if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
       emulate -L sh -o KSH_ARRAYS
   fi
   \```
   (alternative: just use the `${arr[@]}` iteration pattern throughout; index access is only needed for `agents[1]` first-pane setup and the `for j` trim loop — both rewritable).
5. **`local -A seen` (current line 571)** — keep as-is (bash 4+ supports `local -A`).
6. **`unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd` (current line 633)** — works in both shells; keep.

### Removed from sesh-sessions function body

- `zle reset-prompt > /dev/null 2>&1 || true` — drop. ZLE/ble.sh both redraw on widget exit; the line was always defensive (the `|| true`).

### Cross-file updates

- **`docs/shells/aliases.md`** — verify the row(s) for `shere`/`sroot`/`scode`/`svibe`/`sesh-sessions`. If the table has a "source" column listing `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh`, update to `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` (+ note the zsh shim).
- **CLAUDE.md** — no edit needed. The existing three-tier rule already covers this case; we're following it, not changing it.

### Verification

1. `chezmoi diff` — confirm new shared file + slim zsh file + new bash file.
2. `chezmoi apply --dry-run` — no template errors.
3. **zsh check** (in a git repo dir):
   - `source ~/.zshrc` → `svibe --help` prints help; Alt+S launches picker.
   - `svibe --no-attach 2 claude` → `tmux ls` shows `vibe/<repo>` session with 2 agent panes.
4. **bash check** (run `bash` in a tmux pane):
   - `source ~/.bashrc` → `svibe --help` works; `scode --help` works; `shere`, `sroot` work.
   - Alt+S triggers picker (assumes ble.sh attached — which is the configured default per `dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash.tmpl`).
5. **Cross-shell same-session attach**: `svibe` in zsh, then from another pane `bash`, run `svibe` → should attach existing `vibe/<repo>` session, not duplicate.
6. Run `bash --noprofile --norc` then `source ~/.bashrc` cold to confirm no errors at source time on bash 5.x.
